items_missed: Never asked 'how are you today?' — the customer opened with 'hey there, how you doing?' and Dustin answered with 'Okay. What day are you looking to move?' instead of returning the courtesy.

No real agenda statement: 'I'll get some information to get you a profile built and then we can run through the details' gave a rough roadmap but no 10-15 minute timeframe and no 'sound good?' confirmation.

Never asked the moving-stressors question ('is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?') — the customer volunteered two stressors on his own (the heavy adjustable king base, the budget) instead of being invited to.
Never asked about additional stops.
No 'pricing is super simple' opener — jumped straight from 'bear with me just a second' into $200 materials and a $312/hr rate.
Never listed what's included (wrap, pads, bands, tools, taxes, insurance) — only 'no additional drive time, gas time or anything.'

Disassembly/reassembly inclusion never mentioned, despite the customer specifically raising the two-piece adjustable king base and saying 'moving is always... just assembly and all the other bullshit.'
No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) never mentioned — a miss made larger by the fact that a damage-relevant COI conversation happened mid-call.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — notable on a move where the customer has freight elevators reserved in both buildings on a fixed date.
15-minute prorated increments after the 2.5-hour minimum never explained — only 'after that you pay for the time that you use.'
Number of trucks never stated (3-person team was given, truck count was not).
No time equivalents or reference points used to make the hour estimate concrete.

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing — no 'prep before move day = shorter move = lower bill,' no take-a-carload tip even though the customer explicitly offered to handle bathroom items, food and supplies himself.
'No deposit required' never mentioned.
No mention of the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email and no 'reply with any corrections' ask.
No final 'any other questions before I let you go?' — the only question invite was pricing-specific and came mid-call.
Business hours and how to reach us never given.
Customer's name used once (at spelling confirmation) and never again — 'man' and 'sir' carried the whole call.
No Ecobox referral, which was directly on point: the customer asked for unpacking and box disposal and got a flat 'we don't offer unpacking or the disposal' with no alternative offered.
No insurance explanation at all (No Worries or the 60c/lb baseline).
Repeated dead air fighting the estimating tool — 'our software is very finicky,' 'it is still not showing me the total, I'm sorry man' — right at the pricing reveal, the worst possible moment.
top_strength: The discovery and the estimate build were genuinely strong. Dustin got origin and destination addresses with zip and unit, square footage, floors at both ends (33rd to 8th), walk distance, special/heavy items, additional space, and packing needs, and he handled the hardest question in the call well — he pre-loaded the box count with a benchmark ('generally on a 1600 square foot apartment, we'd expect to pack up around fifty to sixty boxes') so the customer could react instead of guess. He also showed his math out loud when the customer pushed back on 6.5 hours to pack, explaining he took the man hours and added a third mover, and he framed the number honestly: 'I'm definitely trying to give you like a worst case scenario estimate but I'd rather you get sticker shock on this side of the conversation.' Local credibility landed too — 'I've definitely done moves over there in that building' and correctly guessing the 70-foot walk.
coaching_note: Dustin, the highest-leverage fix is the differentiator block — you gave this customer a price and nothing to weigh it against, which is exactly why the number felt 'a little high' to him. Right after the rate, say: 'Pricing is super simple — that rate covers the truck, gas, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands and tools, plus disassembly and reassembly, and there are no hidden fees. You're also covered by our No Worries Damage Coverage, up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse accidental damage. A few days out you'll get a Meet Your Mover email with your mover's photo and info, and we back an On-Time Guarantee — if we miss your window, we start discounting immediately.' On a 33rd-floor-to-8th-floor move with reserved freight elevators, the On-Time Guarantee alone would have been worth real money to him. Second priority: he handed you the budget objection ('I thought it was gonna be closer to $3,200') and you answered with 'you only pay for the time you use' — that's true but passive. That was the cue for Save Your Ass: 'Here's how you actually pull that number down — anything you prep before we get there is time we don't bill. Consolidate the loose stuff in drawers, get the photos off the walls, and take a carload of the bathroom and pantry items yourself. Does that make sense?' He had already volunteered to do exactly that, so you were pushing on an open door. Third, close it properly — no deposit required, the bolded detail list at the top of the email, reply with any corrections, hours and how to reach you, and use his name: he told you it was Daniel and you never said it once. One process note: pre-build the estimate range before the pricing reveal so the tool isn't stalling while the customer waits on his number.
phone_presence_notes: Easy, natural rapport — matched the customer's casual register without becoming unprofessional, defused the heavy bed-frame worry with 'we move those all the time, no worries for sure,' and got genuine agreement moments ('Exactly!'), though he never used the customer's name and let the software fumbling create awkward dead air at the pricing reveal.
